edits.fix: Add the packet id on every page: "Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / PCFZV" (template fix covering all five pages).

edits.quote: It is your turn with a bigger pile.
edits.fix: Delete "with a bigger pile"; the pictures already show the piles. Start with "It is your turn.".

edits.quote: Recording space is exactly five rows of 4 counters and exactly eight rows of 5 counters.
edits.fix: The row counts give away how many ways there are (5 and 8), so the child never has to decide when the list is complete. Print extra rows (e.g. 7 and 10) or leave open space so the children decide when they have found every way.

k-1.summary: A strong K-1 sequence: piles 1-12 played out with drawn counters, traps 1-20, a greedy-move check (Ben takes 2), a new rule {1,2,3}, two piles with a copying strategy, and a misere ending. All answers check (traps 3,6,...; 4,8,...; 1,4,7,...; two-pile answers 2nd,1st,2nd,1st,2nd,2nd). Only small fixes: the footer id, a filler phrase, and P6 rows that reveal the count.

edits.fix: Add the packet id on every page: "Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / PCFZV".

edits.quote: In every game in this packet, two players take turns taking counters from a pile. Each problem says how many counters a player may take on a turn.
edits.fix: Cut the meta narration: "Two players take turns taking counters from a pile." Each problem already states its moves.

edits.quote: If you cannot take any counters on your turn, you lose.
edits.fix: This conflicts with P9 (last counter loses): after the loser takes the last counter, the other player faces an empty pile and by this rule would also lose. Limit the sentence to last-counter-wins games, or add to P9 that the game ends as soon as someone takes the last counter.

grades-2-3.summary: Well built around the outline: claims to test against every reply (Lee/Mo, Jo/Kai, where Kai's greedy 4 is wrong), the {1,3,4} classification with period 7 pushed to 30/50/61/100, a parity game, two piles, inventing a rule for multiples of 5, and a misere ending. All answers check (L = 2,7,9,14,16; evens for {1,3,5}; (4,1) a surprise second-player win; misere L = 1,3,8,10,15,17). Only the shared-rules paragraph needs trimming and a fix for the misere conflict, plus the footer id.

edits.fix: Add the packet id on every page: "Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / PCFZV".

edits.quote: In every game in this packet, two players take turns taking counters from a pile. Each problem says how many counters a player may take on a turn.
edits.fix: Cut to "Two players take turns taking counters from a pile." Each problem names its moves.

edits.quote: If you cannot take any counters on your turn, you lose.
edits.fix: This conflicts with P7 (last counter loses), where the player facing the empty pile would then also lose. Say the clause applies when taking the last counter wins, or add to P7 that the game ends when the last counter is taken.

edits.quote: When the two piles are the same size, which player can always win? Explain why.
edits.fix: The shaded grid shows that second wins exactly when the piles leave the same remainder on division by 3 (e.g. 1 and 4, 2 and 5). Asking only about equal piles repeats the 2-3 question and leaves this main pattern unasked. Replace with "Describe every shaded square and explain why the second player wins there."

grades-4-5.summary: Mathematically rich and correct: {1,3,4} to 24 and then to 100/1000/2026 (L, W take 4, W take 3 or 1), four contrasting rules ({1,2,4} matching {1,2}, {1,4} with period 5, parity), greedy failing in all but {1,3,5}, a periodicity proof, a complete classification (the games {1,2,3}, {1,2,3,5}, {1,2,3,6} and {1,2,3,5,6}), a misere shift, and two-pile grids whose {1,3,4} answer (1-3, 1-8, 3-8, 2-7, 4-6) requires real work. Edits are light: footer id, shared-rules wording and misere conflict, and a stronger P8 question.

overall.strongest: The grades 4-5 band develops all three outline kernels (backward induction, periodicity with a proof, rule changes, greedy failure and two-pile sums) through correct, well-ordered problems with proper grids and workspace.
overall.weakest: The shared-rules paragraph in grades 2-3 and 4-5 has meta narration and a cannot-move clause that conflicts with the misere problems, and every footer is missing the packet id.
